greek.definition: Relating to the architecture of ancient Greece, especially its columns, temples, and balanced proportions.

roman.definition: Relating to ancient Roman architecture, known for arches, vaults, domes, concrete, and monumental public buildings.

byzantine.definition: Relating to Byzantine architecture, known for domes, mosaics, and richly decorated religious interiors.

romanesque.definition: A style of architecture developed in Italy and western Europe between the Roman and the Gothic styles after 1000 AD.

gothic.definition: Relating to Gothic architecture, known for pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and large stained-glass windows.

renaissance.definition: An architectural tradition drawing on classical forms and proportion in Renaissance Europe.

baroque.definition: An architectural style emphasizing movement, dramatic spatial effects and rich ornament.

neoclassical.definition: Characteristic of a revival of an earlier classical style.

beaux-arts.definition: A grand style in architecture and the fine arts drew on a Paris school’s classical designs, symmetry, lavish ornament, and monumental scale, flourishing in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

palladian.definition: Referring to or relating to or having the style of architecture created by Andrea Palladio.

art-nouveau.definition: An international art movement from around 1900 brought graceful curves and plant-inspired forms into buildings and everyday objects.

art-deco.definition: A design movement popular during the 1920s and 1930s, known for simplified shapes and geometric patterns suitable for factory production.

bauhaus.definition: A design tradition associated with the Bauhaus school founded in Germany in 1919.

modernist.definition: Relating to modernist architecture, which favors functional forms, simple geometry, and little ornament.

brutalist.definition: Relating to an architectural style known for massive forms, exposed materials, and especially raw concrete.
brutalist.exampleUsage: The museum has a Brutalist exterior with large concrete surfaces.

international-style.definition: A modern architectural style using simple geometric forms, little ornament, and materials such as glass, steel, and concrete.
international-style.exampleUsage: The office tower reflects the International Style with its glass façade and clean lines.

mid-century-modern.definition: Modern design associated with the middle decades of the twentieth century.

postmodern.definition: Architecture that responds to modernism through varied references, forms and ornament.

deconstructivist.definition: Describing architecture with fragmented forms and unexpected angles.

high-tech.definition: An architectural approach that prominently expresses structural and building-service technology.

minimalist.definition: Architecture emphasizing simple forms and a restrained use of elements and materials.

sustainable.definition: Designed to reduce environmental impact and resource use over the building life cycle.

parametric.definition: Designed using relationships between adjustable parameters to generate or control forms.

organic.definition: Relating to architecture designed to harmonize with its site, materials, and natural surroundings.

biophilic.definition: Designed to connect people with plants, natural light, and nature.

smart-building.definition: A building that uses connected systems to control its operations.

adaptive-reuse.definition: The practice of giving an existing building a new purpose.

net-zero.definition: Here, a net-zero-energy building balances annual energy use with renewable energy production under a stated standard.

passive-house.arabicTranslation: منزل منخفض الطاقة وفق نهج باسيف هاوس
passive-house.definition: A building approach using high energy efficiency and envelope performance to reduce heating and cooling demand.

modular.definition: Constructed with standardized units or dimensions allowing flexibility and variety in use.

dome.definition: A rounded roof or ceiling structure, often shaped like part of a sphere.

arch.definition: A curved structural element spanning an opening.

vault.definition: An arched architectural structure forming a ceiling or roof.

cantilever.definition: A beam or structure supported at only one end, projecting outward.

facade.definition: The face or front of a building.

atrium.definition: An open central space within a building, often extending through several floors.

skylight.definition: A window in a roof to admit daylight.

colonnade.definition: Structure consisting of a row of evenly spaced columns.

portico.definition: A porch or entrance to a building consisting of a covered and often columned area.

minaret.definition: A tower associated with a mosque, traditionally used for the call to prayer.
